newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish military in top-level meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkish military in top-level meeting.

text.p: Turkey's influential military top brass began a four-day meeting on Friday at which they were expected to probe members of the ranks suspected of Islamist activism.

The generals posed for television cameras around a table at the armed forces headquarters at the start of their Supreme Military Council, an annual meeting called ostensibly to fix routine personnel issues.
"Dossiers on staff who have been involved in fundamentalist activities will be dealt with along with promotions and retirements," the Milliyet daily said.
The army, which regards itself as the guardian of Turkey's secularist tradition, has sacked dozens of officers at council meetings in recent years.

Pressure from the military was key in the collapse of Islamist former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan's government in June. The army had insisted that Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, crack down on Moslem revivalism.
